title: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Reasoning Models: Language, Multimodality, and Beyond
actual_read_scope: Read the abstract, introduction/figures, §2 framing of token efficiency, §6 Efficient Reasoning during Pretraining (6.1 latent space, 6.2 subquadratic attention, 6.3 linearization, 6.4 efficient reasoning with subquadratic attention), §7 outlook/evaluation where it clarifies token-quality evidence, and the direct reference entries for the selected pretraining/architecture works. Did not read any cited original paper. Earlier inference/SFT/RL sections were not re-read except where needed to distinguish pretraining claims.

routes.problem: Standard CoT makes reasoning cost grow with generated intermediate tokens and long-context attention.
routes.mechanism: The survey organizes pretraining methods around latent-space reasoning, subquadratic attention/linear sequence models, and linearization of pretrained Transformers.
routes.inference_token_connection: Latent or sentence/concept-level units can reduce explicit textual intermediate tokens, but the survey mostly argues computational/memory efficiency and does not establish matched-accuracy output-token savings for general reasoning.

routes.problem: A model may be trained to reason in a compressed latent representation rather than emitting every step as text.
routes.mechanism: Latent thought vectors, latent/concept tokens, and mixed latent/text objectives replace or interleave discrete CoT with continuous hidden-state representations.
routes.inference_token_connection: Potentially direct for visible reasoning-token reduction, but evidence in this survey is qualitative or framed as sample/computation efficiency; it does not provide a task-level quality-versus-output-token curve.

routes.problem: Long reasoning traces create quadratic attention and KV/memory overhead.
routes.mechanism: Linear attention, SSM/RNN-like models, sparse attention, and Transformer-to-linear distillation reduce sequence-processing complexity while retaining pretrained knowledge.
routes.inference_token_connection: Compute_only unless a cited work measures fewer generated tokens: these methods reduce per-token cost/long-context memory, not necessarily the number of reasoning tokens needed for a correct answer.

routes.problem: Pretraining architecture can affect reasoning quality under a fixed compute budget.
routes.mechanism: Distilled subquadratic models and hybrid Mamba/MLP/Transformer backbones are presented as ways to generate multiple reasoning paths faster and retain reasoning quality.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect: faster or cheaper multi-path generation may permit a different token budget, but the survey does not claim fewer final reasoning tokens at matched quality.

candidates.title: Byte latent transformer: patches scale better than tokens
candidates.reason: Entropy-based byte patches replace fixed tokenizer units and are described as reducing computational overhead; the survey does not show fewer reasoning/output tokens at matched quality.

candidates.title: Large concept models: language modeling in a sentence representation space
candidates.authors: L. The, L. Barrault, P. Duquenne et al.
candidates.reason: Sentence-level concepts become autoregressive units, which can shorten explicit textual reasoning traces; no task-level token-quality evidence is given in this survey.

candidates.title: Token assorted: mixing latent and text tokens for improved language model reasoning
candidates.authors: D. Su, H. Zhu, Y. Xu et al.
candidates.reason: Mixed latent/text representations are explicitly presented as reducing memory and computational cost; the survey does not establish fewer visible reasoning tokens for equal accuracy.

candidates.title: Latent thought models
candidates.reason: The survey says latent thought vectors guide token generation and allow adjustment of inference steps/dimensions; this is the clearest pretraining-to-inference-token connection, but no exact benchmark curve or identifier is supplied in the survey text.

candidates.title: Thinking slow, fast: scaling inference compute with distilled reasoners
candidates.reason: The survey reports distilled Mamba models enabling faster multi-path CoT under fixed compute and improved MATH/GSM8K performance; this is compute/throughput evidence, not proof of fewer generated tokens.

candidates.title: Compositional reasoning with transformers, rnns, and chain of thought
candidates.authors: G. Yehudai, N. Amsel, J. Bruna
candidates.reason: Provides formal complexity trade-offs among Transformers, RNNs, and CoT-augmented models; it informs architecture cost, not an empirical reduction in required reasoning tokens.

candidates.title: Mamba-2: the new SSM architecture
candidates.reason: The survey presents Mamba2/state-space duality as improving hardware efficiency and supporting recurrent inference; it reduces per-token/sequence cost rather than token count.

candidates.title: Transformers to SSMs: distilling quadratic knowledge to subquadratic models
candidates.authors: A. Bick, K. Li, E. Xing, J. Z. Kolter, A. Gu
candidates.reason: MOHAWK is cited for distilling pretrained Transformer knowledge into subquadratic models; the claimed benefit is efficient inference, with no fewer-output-token claim in this survey.

classification_gaps: The pretraining section is primarily an architectural and sequence-complexity taxonomy. It does not separate visible reasoning-token reduction from lower FLOPs/KV/memory per token.
No pretraining recipe is shown to produce a calibrated task-dependent stopping policy; adaptive token allocation appears mainly in inference/RL sections, outside this requested pretraining read.
evidence_conflicts: The abstract and §2 define efficiency using quality divided by cost, where cost may include generated tokens, FLOPs, or latency; §6 evidence mostly concerns FLOPs, memory, throughput, or asymptotic sequence cost.
Latent/concept-level methods may hide reasoning in continuous states rather than remove computation; visible-token savings must not be treated as total reasoning-cost savings.
training_only_or_compute_only: Linear attention, SSMs, sparse attention, linearization, and Transformer distillation are compute_only unless an original paper reports matched-quality token counts.
BLT's patch/token processing and LCM's sentence units concern representation granularity; the survey does not show that a task needs fewer semantic reasoning steps.
gaps_conflicts.pretraining_answer: Pretraining can influence inference efficiency by changing the unit of prediction (bytes, concepts, latent vectors), internalizing some reasoning, or enabling subquadratic architectures. In this survey, only latent/concept approaches have a plausible direct connection to fewer visible reasoning tokens; the reported evidence is not sufficient to claim a validated quality-preserving token reduction. Most §6 claims are compute_only or indirect.
gaps_conflicts.security_resource_waste: This survey does discuss overthinking, redundant reasoning, and long-CoT safety in §§2 and 7, but the requested pretraining section does not connect security attacks to token waste. Safety/overthinking evidence belongs to other lifecycle stages.
